summary: This document specifies how to encapsulate ATM cells in a pseudowire carried over an MPLS network, along with the procedures for using such a pseudowire to provide an ATM service. This lets service providers offer emulated ATM services over existing MPLS networks.

plainLanguage.summary: Old ATM networks had their own kind of mail envelope. This shows how to carry those envelopes through a newer network so customers don't have to replace their old equipment.

questions: how does atm over mpls work
what is the pseudowire control word
subtitle: How to carry ATM cells and AAL5 frames across an MPLS network inside a pseudowire.

tldr.problem: Service providers with ATM customers want to run those services over a single packet-switched MPLS core without making customers change their ATM equipment.
tldr.mechanism: An ATM pseudowire wraps ATM cells, or whole AAL5 frames, behind an MPLS pseudowire label and a small control word. RFC 4717 defines four encapsulation modes, with N-to-one cell mode as the only required one.
tldr.outcome: ATM can be emulated over MPLS, though not perfectly: cell ordering, QoS and flow control behave differently from native ATM.

today: RFC 4717 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The RFC itself notes that early ATM PW implementations without a control word existed, and requires future ones to remain compatible with them.

sections.title: ATM Service Over a Packet Network
sections.content:
Packet Switched Networks (PSNs) can let almost any existing digital service run over one network infrastructure. For a provider this means using existing systems to get more capacity from a packet core, keeping the operational processes used for legacy services, and using one infrastructure for both old and new services.

RFC 4717 describes how to carry ATM over MPLS. Two edge routers, called Provider Edge (PE) devices, are joined by a pseudowire (PW) inside a PSN tunnel. The customer devices (CE) on each side are not aware that they use an emulated service instead of a native one.

The RFC is upfront that this is not perfect emulation. Cell ordering can be kept only through the optional sequence field, and using it may affect ATM quality of service. ATM flow control is transparent to the MPLS network and cannot reflect its status. Control-plane support for ATM SVCs, SVPs, SPVCs and SPVPs is out of scope. The encapsulations are identical to those in ITU-T Y.1411 and Y.1412.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine an old postal system with its own little envelopes. Instead of replacing it, you tuck each envelope inside a parcel for a bigger delivery network. It works well, but it is not exactly the same as the old system.

sections.title: The Encapsulation and Its Control Word
sections.content:
Every packet has a PSN transport header (which depends on the tunneling technology), a pseudowire header, an ATM control word and the ATM service payload. With MPLS, the pseudowire header is one or more labels at the bottom of the label stack, and the ingress router MUST set the S bit of the PW label to 1.

There are two control word layouts, both based on RFC 4385. The generic control word (used by one-to-one cell mode and AAL5 PDU mode) has four zero bits, 4 reserved bits, a 16-bit sequence number and 8 ATM-specific bits. The preferred control word (used by N-to-one cell mode and AAL5 SDU mode) has four zero bits, 4 flag bits, 2 reserved bits, a 6-bit length and a 16-bit sequence number.

The length field exists because some links, such as Ethernet with its 64-octet minimum frame, pad short packets. If the packet length is under 64 bytes, the length is set to it; otherwise it is zero. In N-to-one mode it MUST be 0.

The sequence number is a 16-bit circular space, its processing is optional, and the value 0 means sequence checking is not used. If a PE negotiated not to process sequence numbers and receives a non-zero one, it SHOULD send a PW status message indicating a receive fault and disable the PW.

The control word is useful against ECMP load balancing: a router may look at the first nibble after the label stack to guess whether the packet is IP, so an ATM VPI starting with 0x4 or 0x6 could be mistaken for IPv4 or IPv6 when no control word is present. Where it is not otherwise required it is optional, but future implementations MUST be able to send and receive frames without one, for compatibility with early deployments. The PEs must know whether a control word is in use, by configuration or by signaling as in RFC 4447.
sections.plainLanguage: The control word is a small label stuck on each parcel. It can say how long the parcel is and its place in line, so the other end can spot parcels that arrive out of order.

sections.title: The Four Encapsulation Modes
sections.content:
Two ways of mapping ATM connections are defined. In N-to-one mode, one or more virtual channel connections (VCCs) or virtual path connections (VPCs) share one pseudowire and the 4-octet ATM header is kept unchanged. This is the only REQUIRED mode. In one-to-one mode, a single VCC or VPC maps to one pseudowire, and the VPI/VCI can be derived from the PW label, so it saves bandwidth. It is OPTIONAL.

For AAL5 traffic, two OPTIONAL frame modes exist. The AAL5 SDU mode reassembles each frame and carries only its payload, which is more efficient for small frames but needs segmentation and reassembly at the PE. The AAL5 PDU mode carries the whole frame, including padding and trailer, and is transparent to ATM OAM and security applications.

Each mode has limits. Cell modes cannot translate the EFCI congestion bit into a PSN equivalent, cannot match the ATM header error correction, and support only point-to-point LSPs. The SDU mode can reorder OAM cells, cannot handle scrambled PDUs, does not carry the AAL5 CRC (the egress PE must regenerate it), and does not preserve CLP and EFCI for every cell.
sections.plainLanguage: You can ship the little envelopes one by one, many together, or you can wait until a whole letter is complete and ship it as one package. Each way has its own trade-off between speed and keeping everything exactly the same.

sections.title: Cell Modes in Detail
sections.content:
In N-to-one cell mode, each cell is sent as its 4-byte ATM header (without the header error check) plus its 48-byte payload. A frame is a multiple of 52 bytes, and the number of cells is inferred from the frame length. The ingress router MUST NOT send more cells than the egress router is willing to receive, a number that is configured or signaled. Putting several cells in one frame is called cell concatenation and adds latency and delay variation. When several VCCs or VPCs share a PW, their VPI/VCI values MUST be unique.

Edge routers MAY change the EFCI bit from zero to one to reflect known congestion, and the CLP bit from zero to one to reflect edge policing, but SHOULD NOT change either from one to zero.

In one-to-one mode, the generic control word is REQUIRED. Each cell carries an ATM-specific byte with the M bit (cell or AAL5 payload), the V bit (whether a VCI is present), a 3-bit PTI and the CLP bit. A VCC service leaves out the VCI, while a VPC service sends a 16-bit VCI with each cell. When several cells share a packet, the ATM-specific byte is repeated for each cell, so 49 bytes carry each 53-byte cell for a VCC and 51 bytes for a VPC. The ingress and egress PEs MUST agree on a maximum cell count, by signaling or configuration. A VPC service emulates a Virtual Path cross-connect, and the egress PE MUST NOT change the VCI.
sections.plainLanguage: Each little envelope can travel with a short note on top. If you only ship envelopes for one customer, you can skip writing the customer's address on each one, since the parcel already says who it is for.

sections.title: AAL5 Frame Modes and Fragmentation
sections.content:
In AAL5 SDU mode, the ingress PE reassembles the frame, drops the padding and trailer, and sends only the payload. The egress PE MUST regenerate the padding and trailer. The control word has flag bits: T (1 means an ATM admin cell follows, otherwise AAL5 payload), E (EFCI), C (CLP) and U (the Frame Relay command/response bit used with Frame Relay/ATM interworking). OAM cells that arrive during reassembly are sent immediately, so strict OAM ordering is not kept.

In AAL5 PDU mode, the whole CPCS-PDU, including the padding and trailer, is carried unprocessed, so even a frame with an invalid CRC or length is transported. One reason given is that a security agent may have scrambled the cell payloads. The generic control word is MANDATORY here, and the U, E and C bits describe the last cell's User-to-User bit, the EFCI state and the cell loss priority.

If the ingress PE cannot reassemble a full frame, because the PDU exceeds the PW MTU or OAM cells arrive mid-frame, it fragments the PDU. Fragmentation always happens at cell boundaries. If an OAM or RM cell arrives, the PE sends the current frame and then the OAM or RM cell using one-to-one single cell encapsulation. In the other direction, the egress PE rebuilds each cell's PTI field from the E and U bits and sets CLP from the C bit.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of mailing every small envelope, you can wait for a whole letter to be finished and mail it as a single package. If something urgent arrives in the middle, you send the package so far and then the urgent note straight away.

sections.title: OAM Cells and Defect Handling
sections.content:
OAM (Operations And Maintenance) cells carry alarms and tests inside ATM. For a VCC service, both PEs SHOULD act as a VC switch and SHOULD pass F5 AIS, RDI, loopback, resource management, performance management, continuity check and security cells transparently. For a VPC service, the PEs SHOULD act as a VP cross-connect and handle F4 AIS, RDI and loopback cells, and MUST pass the F5 cell types transparently. A PE configured as an administrative segment boundary SHOULD terminate segment OAM cells.

A PE in SDU or PDU mode that does not carry OAM cells MAY emulate OAM support. It loops back an F5 end-to-end loopback cell with indication value 1 after decrementing it, notifies the remote PE of AIS alarms and interface failures, and generates an F5 AIS on affected PVCs when it detects a PW failure such as a label withdraw, a failed LDP session or a PW status notification.

Defects can occur on the CE-to-PE link, on the ATM side of the PW, on the PSN side of the PE or inside the PSN. For lower-layer defects the ingress PE MUST be able to generate an F4 AIS for a VPC and SHOULD generate an F5 AIS for a VCC. For PSN failures, the egress PE SHOULD generate the matching AIS. If a PW fails in one direction, the whole bidirectional service is considered failed.
sections.plainLanguage: OAM cells are like checkup messages that say whether the line is working. The two edge routers either pass them along or fake the replies themselves, and they raise an alarm if the road between them breaks.

sections.title: Class of Service, ILMI and Congestion
sections.content:
Section 12 is guidance only and is not part of the standard. The ATM service category of a connection SHOULD be mapped to a compatible class of service in the PSN. For example, CBR SHOULD map to a class with stringent loss and delay objectives, such as one based on the EF PHB in a Diffserv network. On MPLS, the CLP bit can be mapped to the EXP field, but the details are outside the scope.

An MPLS edge PE MAY provide the ATM Integrated Local Management Interface (ILMI). If the PE learns that the ATM edge switch deleted a VC, or the physical interface goes down, it MUST send a PW status notification for all affected PWs, and the egress PE MUST then delete the VC using ILMI.

The RFC defines one ATM-specific interface parameter sub-TLV, type 0x02: a 2-octet maximum number of concatenated ATM cells. An ingress PE can concatenate up to this value but MUST NOT exceed it.

ATM PWs may not be TCP-friendly, and where they consume more than their fair share they SHOULD be halted. They should run over traffic-engineered PSNs where possible, and PEs SHOULD monitor for congestion. A PW can be restarted manually or automatically after a waiting time.
sections.plainLanguage: Important traffic should get a fast lane on the bigger network. If the road gets too crowded, the sender should be told to pause, then try again after a while.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
RFC 4717 specifies only encapsulations, not the protocols that carry the encapsulated packets across the PSN. Each such protocol may have its own security issues, but they are not affected by these encapsulations.

The security of the transported ATM service is only as good as the security of the PSN, and that level might be less rigorous than a native ATM service.
sections.plainLanguage: Your parcel is only as safe as the delivery network that carries it, and that network may be less locked down than the old one.
